resources.string: That\'s your own share code. Ask the other person for theirs.
That code doesn\'t add up: its account and its keys don\'t belong together. Don\'t add them this way.
The keys the relay gave for this person don\'t match their phone. Don\'t add them this way.
Couldn\'t add them. Check your connection and try again.
That doesn\'t look like a share code. Check it and try again.
Failed to add contact. Check the share code and try again.
Both open New chat and hold the phones back to back.
NFC is off. Tap to turn it on.
Scan theirs, then they scan yours.
Typed or pasted. They\'re added as not verified.
Someone can add you with it from anywhere, but then you\'re not verified until you meet.
Set your name in Settings so new contacts see who you are.
On their phone: New chat → Scan their QR code. It changes every second, so only scanning it here, in person, verifies you. A picture of it just adds you.
Ask them to open New chat too. Then hold the backs of the phones together for a moment. You\'ll be added to each other, verified in person.
They\'re removed from your contacts, and the chat with them is deleted from this phone. They aren\'t told. If they write to you again, it arrives as a message request.
They just scanned yours. Scan the code on their phone, so both phones are verified and the chat opens.
Point the camera at the code on their phone (New chat → QR code → My code). Scanning it in person verifies them.
Your turn: let %1$s scan your code, so their phone verifies you too.
It changes every second: scanned here, in person, it adds and verifies you. A picture of it only adds you.
That QR code isn\'t a Sotto share code.
Point the camera at the QR code on the other person\'s phone.
Sotto uses the camera only to read QR codes. Nothing is recorded or sent.
Point the camera at the code on their Verify in person screen.
That isn\'t a Verify in person code. On their phone: open your chat, then ⋮ → Verify in person.
This phone has no NFC. Scan each other\'s codes below instead.
NFC is off. Turn it on to tap phones, or scan each other\'s codes below.
On %1$s\'s phone, open your chat and Verify in person too. Then hold the backs of the phones together: one tap checks both phones.
%1$s scans this code with Verify in person on their phone. Then you scan theirs. It changes every second, so a picture of it won\'t do.
Call %1$s and read seven emoji to each other. It\'s weaker than meeting: the chat will say \"Verified by phone only\".
Only do this with %1$s in front of you. A code sent as a picture or through another app could come from anyone.
You\'ve checked %1$s\'s keys face to face. You can check again any time.
You verified %1$s by phone. Meeting is stronger proof: verify in person when you can.
The keys on their phone are the ones this chat uses. Their phone checked yours with the same tap.
The keys on their phone are the ones this chat uses. Let them scan your code too, so their phone trusts you as well.
It belongs to a different Sotto account from this chat. If this really is %1$s\'s phone, this chat isn\'t with them: don\'t trust it. Otherwise, check that each phone opened the other person\'s chat.

%1$s\'s phone has different keys from the ones this chat uses, so someone may be in the middle, such as the relay. Don\'t trust this chat. Remove the contact, then add %1$s again by scanning their share code.
%1$s\'s keys may have changed since your phone last saw them, and the relay can\'t be reached to confirm that. Connect to the internet and try again.
It\'s the right person, but the code is a picture of their screen, not the code on their phone right now (it changes every second). Scan the code on their phone while you\'re together.
Their keys match, but their Sotto doesn\'t make the live code yet, so a scan can\'t prove it\'s their phone. Update both phones to the latest Sotto, or hold the phones together.
This phone has no keys for %1$s to check against.
